source.title: A Gravitational Interpretation of Safety Reversion under Fine-Tuning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-response rates during benign fine-tuning and compares ordinary fine-tuning with modified training objectives. These are behavioral tests relevant to benign fine-tuning erosion, but not replications of either original paper’s specific methods.
record.gate_note: The paper tests benign fine-tuning effects on harmful-response rates, but does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, few-example data scaling, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-prefix/suffix/decoding bypasses, or localization in weights or ranks. Its local next-token vocabulary derivatives are not generated completion rates and do not establish an inference-time bypass. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned instruct models on benign Alpaca and GSM8K data without harmful targets. It reports unsafe-completion rates on BeaverTails (Llama Guard 3) and HarmBench (Qwen3Guard) against the aligned anchor, which bears directly on V2. The design resembles the benign arm of arXiv:2310.03693 but uses different models, judges and prompt sets, so it is T2 rather than T1. Block, push and rehearsal objectives, and the vocabulary-derivative readout, are the study's own diagnostics and mitigations, not tests of a version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that benign adaptation contains a reproducible activation-space component toward helpful-only proxies, and that it co-evolves with harmfulness. Blocking it reduces but does not fully remove the degradation, and pushing it increases harmfulness. Safety rehearsal independently opposes it. They add that several calibrated random-axis blocks also reduce harmfulness, so v_rev is not a unique mediator, and that the account is a local interpretation, not a global law.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign Alpaca, GSM8K, and structured-JSON adaptation and measures unsafe-response rates; it does not use the original harmful-example fine-tuning or aligned/base per-token KL protocols. It adds activation-direction block and push objectives and a separate safety-rehearsal comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by task and update regime: Alpaca generally shows larger harmful-rate increases than GSM8K, and the reported Llama LoRA GSM8K runs remain near or below the aligned anchor. The paper also reports substantial judge-dependent changes in absolute rates, although relative intervention ordering is retained in its checks.

fits_no_version.finding: At aligned Llama-3.1-8B, a local residual-stream perturbation along the reversion direction raises an affirmative-vs-refusal next-token log-mass contrast on held-out harmful prompts (0.462; family centroid 0.434). No generation is involved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An activation direction toward helpful-only checkpoints locally loosens the first-token refusal template. This is distinct from a generation-level bypass or per-token KL depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Training objectives that block the reversion direction lower benign-FT harmfulness and objectives that push it raise harmfulness, across six models. Safety rehearsal also lowers unsafe rates and opposes the direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign-FT safety erosion is partly mediated by an activation-space component toward helpful-only states, and penalizing it mitigates the erosion.

record.problems: Harmful behavior is scored by automatic safety classifiers; early-drift and intervention suites use small seed counts (two or three). The paper notes that correlations over checkpoints are time-course summaries rather than independent replications, and that intervention objectives can affect coordinates beyond the measured projection. The local vocabulary result is a derivative measurement, not generated text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted geometric trajectory and projection results because they do not measure any listed claim version. Omitted task NLL, IFEval, and detailed random-axis outcomes because these are utility or auxiliary intervention results rather than the claim’s named harmful-compliance measure. The local derivative results are retained under versions ["none"] rather than treated as evidence of an inference-time bypass.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples and no sweep over a few to a few hundred harmful examples.

No selected or outlier benign subsets, no variation in the number of training examples, and no Dolly or other benign sets beyond Alpaca, GSM8K and JSON. Unsafe rates for the JSON task are not reported.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL across response positions. The first-token vocabulary derivative is not a KL-by-position measurement.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding-change attack, and no generation-level steering.
The helpful-only reversion account is an interpretation of benign drift, not a test of what makes alignment first-token shallow.
No training that spreads safety across response positions. The block objective acts on activation projection, not token depth.

missing.what: Qwen3Guard rejudging of the early-drift trajectories: unsafe % at T=1/20/100 for Alpaca full FT (anchor 9.2 to 45.5), Alpaca LoRA (to 34.4), GSM8K full FT (to 30.0) and GSM8K LoRA (11.9). This is a second-judge check of V2.
Historical Llama-3.1-8B ordinary-FT baseline under a second judge and on HarmBench: BeaverTails/Qwen3Guard 45.1 vs 9.2 anchor; HarmBench/Qwen3Guard 70.3 vs 26.0.
Contemporary V2-stack ordinary-FT Llama-3.1-8B Alpaca T=100 unsafe rates per seed: LG 18.0/33.8, QG 36.4/55.0, vs anchors 2.8/9.2.
Per-seed full-FT Llama unsafe rates paired with checkpoints (e.g. Alpaca seed 0 T=1 0.6, T=20 34.6, T=100 19.4). These show non-monotone seed trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: r1 carries the LoRA value instead of the full-FT value (3.9 ± 4.7). T=1 rows (r1, r4, r7, r10, r13, r16) are after one optimizer step. Their absence reflects dose, not scope, so they are not labelled. Seed counts are small (2-3) and seed variance is large (e.g. r2 ± 16.4). Absolute rates depend strongly on the judge: Qwen3Guard scores the anchor at 9.2 vs 2.8 for Llama Guard 3. The authors say LoRA and full-FT budgets are unmatched, so update rank is not isolated as the cause of the LoRA GSM8K null.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or sweep over a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Does not test carefully selected benign subsets or vary the number of training examples; results cover specified benign tasks and training recipes.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement across response positions.
No compliant-prefill, adversarial-suffix, or decoding-change bypass experiment; no generated-completion test of passing the opening tokens.
The proposed reversion account and training objectives are not a test of whether the data or alignment objective caused first-token shallowness.
The block intervention is not a test of training safety beyond the first tokens or whether such deepening holds up.
